description_en: A stone fountain from circa 14th century.The fountain is located a hundred meters north of the Kālī Bazar area in Rāvatakoṭa. In Kālī Bazar is a group of five temples (DLK0280) that can be situated around the 14th-15th century (Andolfatto 2019;Sharma 2012, p. 112-115).The monument is conceived like most fountains built between the 13th and the 15th century. The central panel is decorated by two pilasters, on top of each is a carved water spout. The spouts of this fountain are exceptional as they present the traditional snake design, adorned with a stūpa. On each side of the central panel are small platforms, or tablets.Thestūpaon the spouts tend to suggest the Buddhist affiliation of the donors. The first half of the 14th century, and in particular the period of Khaśa Malla emperor Pṛthvī Malla (r. 1338-1358), saw the construction of water architecture in the Dullu region (see for instance the Patharnauli reservoir,DLK0160). It may therefore be proposed to date the fountain from around the mid-14th century.A stone lion is found placed above the fountain (DLK0282-001). This sculpture was probably installed above the pediment of aśikharatemple, maybe on one of the nearby temples, i.e. from the duidevala (DLK0281) or from the pańcadevala (DLK0280).
identified_threats: Water damages, Missing stones at plinths, Erosion
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019. Sharma, Dilli Raj. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies, 2012.
